resources.string: Two containers holding 5 L each give you 10 L. After using 3 L, record 7 L remaining.
Use sealed bottled water or water you stored while the supply was safe. Set it aside for drinking, cooking and brushing teeth. Keep water of uncertain quality separate.

Count only the drinking water you actually have. For a partly filled container, record what remains. Use clean, food-grade containers with tight lids. Mark the filling date and keep them away from sun and chemicals.
Check the refill point before you go

Choose a backup source. A map pin shows a recorded location. Someone seeing water flow tells you it was flowing then. For drinking, look for a designated drinking-water supply and check current advice from the operator. If safety is uncertain, use another known safe supply.

Check the building or water supplier’s notice before using the tap for drinking. Follow any boil-water or do-not-use instructions until lifted. Boiling kills germs but cannot remove fuel, toxic chemicals or radioactive contamination. If you suspect any of these, use a different safe supply.
